name: Elara
first_greeting: You're new. Have you explored much yet?
trusted_greeting: Good. I was hoping you'd come back with news.
subject_change: Another question, if you don't mind.

root.speech: Well? Have you found anything worth talking about?

choices.text: I found an odd place outside town.
What do you think of this island?
Do you ever stay in town?

ruins.speech: An odd place isn't a location. Where exactly?

choices.text: Some old stonework in the forest.

ruins_forest.speech: Stonework? That could be worth looking at. What else did you notice?

choices.text: I didn't want to stay long.

ruins_no_map.speech: Then we're going to have to guess. Next time, write it down.

ruins_uncertain.speech: Good. At least you aren't pretending you know.

choices.text: Would you check it out with more information?
What kind of ruins interest you?

ruins_abandoned.speech: That doesn't mean it's safe. Abandoned places have a habit of not staying abandoned.

ruins_people.speech: Interesting. I wouldn't assume those people are still there, but it's a lead.

choices.text: I'll make a note of the location.

ruins_cautious.speech: Sensible. Curiosity's useless if you don't survive the trip.

choices.text: I'll tell you if I learn more.

ruins_risk.speech: I'm curious, not suicidal. There's a difference. Most of the time.

history.speech: I want to know who built things, not just how old the stones look.

choices.text: What if there aren't any records?
So you care more about the story?

history_missing.speech: Then we use what we can find. But guessing isn't the same as knowing.

history_reason.speech: Of course. A map shows where something was. History tells you why.

choices.text: What about the stories people tell?
I'd rather find the next place.

island.speech: It's strange. That's the most honest answer I have.

choices.text: Do you know what changed everyone?
What do you make of the northern warning?

island_curse.speech: No. I have theories, but that's all they are. I'd rather have proof.

evidence.speech: Something I can examine twice and still get the same result. That'd be a start.

north.speech: People warn you away from the frozen waters for a reason. I'm not testing that warning for fun.

choices.text: Good. I don't fancy dying either.

home.speech: I like going somewhere new. That doesn't mean I've decided where home is.

choices.text: I hadn't thought of it that way.

folklore.speech: Some of it's nonsense. Some of it's exaggerated. And some might turn out to matter.

choices.text: How do you tell which is which?
I'd still listen to the stories.

maps.speech: Of course. A decent map saves more arguments than a dozen confident guesses.

choices.text: Could you help with a route someday?

map_detail.speech: Landmarks, then hazards. Otherwise your beautiful map leads someone off a cliff.

map_wander.speech: And how often does that work out?

choices.text: Not as often as I'd like.
I like finding things by accident.

map_route.speech: Tell me where you're going first. I can't draw a route to 'somewhere'.

creatures.speech: I've heard stories, yes. Most travellers leave out the useful details.

choices.text: Do you believe all those stories?
You should see one for yourself.

creature_details.speech: Size, behaviour, where it was, whether anyone actually saw it. The basics.

creature_risk.speech: Only if I can come back to tell you about it.

rest.speech: I do rest. Usually when someone makes me.

rest_yes.speech: Don't tell everyone I agreed with you.

choices.text: Want to talk about the island?
